method: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across all cells; strongest FDR-significant cells grouped into adjacent same-sign regions; regions ranked by cluster mass (|area-weighted mean trend| x area).

hotspots.description: Increase in temperature: +1.00 °C/decade on average over 1714 cells (about 1,311,026 km²), +4.40 °C over 1981-2025. Every cell passes FDR significance.
Increase in temperature: +0.81 °C/decade on average over 1015 cells (about 597,549 km²), +3.54 °C over 1981-2025. Every cell passes FDR significance.
Increase in temperature: +0.78 °C/decade on average over 87 cells (about 104,031 km²), +3.45 °C over 1981-2025. Every cell passes FDR significance.

limitations: Hotspots are leads to investigate, not findings; significance does not prove causation.
Based on MERRA-2 reanalysis, whose trends can be affected by changes in the observing systems it assimilates, especially for precipitation and humidity.
Neighbouring cells are spatially correlated, so FDR control is approximate and regions are not independent tests.
Ranking favours large regions with strong trends; it does not measure how unusual a trend is relative to natural variability.
Regions are identified by coordinates only; no place names are assigned.
